The environmental and natural resource economics major integrates the natural sciences with economics to help us understand why many of earth’s natural resources are under threat and how we can design policies to address these threats.
This major teaches students to weigh options and make important decisions concerning the protection, restoration, development, and use of our natural resources.

The degree requires a minimum of 120 credits, including 24 credits in concentration.

The major also requires a minimum of three credits in written communication skills (WRT) at the 200 level or higher.
